answer: The prover commits to a set inclusion proof over the registry of claimants, and the proof is small because it carries the exclusion of every competing holder, so two identities claiming the same resource would have to produce contradictory proofs. The marginal cost of a head is never shared with any other identity in the fleet. Each identity claims a reef, publishes a nectar that no other holder can publish, and is checked against the kernel: a fleet sharing one reef cannot produce two valid nectar proofs, and the kernel records the collision.
